haiku-low.q1: Pull requests run build (not pushed) and unit tests only, and never deploy. A merge to main starts the full pipeline.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA>. It is built once per run; nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry, then fails the run if it fails again. Unit test failure fails the run with no retry. Nothing reaches staging.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the image it ran before this run, restored by deploy.sh rollback staging. That image is found in SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers members who are not the commit author may approve, in the CI UI. If no approval comes within 72 hours, the run expires and nothing reaches production.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store under /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, after a successful stable rollout or on rollback. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable deployment is untouched, SSM tags are unchanged, and the schema stays migrated (forward-only, not reverted). Canary-off runs.
haiku-low.q8: It is cancelled as superseded and posts a notice to #deploys. This covers runs waiting for approval, the window, or the lock.
haiku-low.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until it is inside Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC and the production lock is free. Approvals do not expire.
haiku-low.q10: Canary 5xx ratio from Prometheus, queried every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. One reading above 1%, or a query with no data, fails it and triggers canary-off.
haiku-low.q11: The run posts a waiting-for-approval notice to #deploys with IMAGE_TAG, a smoke results link, and commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG.
haiku-low.q12: Staging and production use kubectl rollout undo; production then runs canary-off. Staging avoids rollback because it would go one version too far back. Production reason: NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: A pull request runs build (image not pushed) and unit tests only, posting status on the PR; it never deploys. A merge to main starts the full pipeline.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the image built once per run, registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA> (IMAGE_TAG). Nothing is rebuilt after tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry; if the retry fails the run fails. Unit test failure gets no retry and fails the run. Any final failure ends the run, nothing reaches staging, and the failing step is posted to the deploys channel.
sonnet.q4: deploy.sh rollback staging runs, setting staging back to SSM previous_tag, the image staging ran before this run. It is found in SSM Parameter Store at /deploy/staging/previous_tag. The run then fails and posts the failing step.
sonnet.q5: Members of release-approvers who are not the commit author, approving in the CI UI. If nobody approves within 72 hours (clock starts at the gate) the run ends as expired: a notice is posted to the deploys channel, nothing goes to production, and staging keeps the image.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store under /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them: after a successful stable rollout (deploy.sh <env> <tag>), and on deploy.sh rollback <env> (current_tag set back to previous_tag). The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment untouched, SSM tags unchanged, and the schema stays migrated (migrations are not reverted). deploy.sh canary-off is run, then the production lock is released and the failure is posted.
sonnet.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded and posts a notice, as long as it has not started its production deploy (including while waiting for approval, the window or the lock).
sonnet.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until it is inside the start window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) and the production lock is free. The approval does not expire (e.g. Thursday evening approval starts Monday 09:00). Once started it may run past 15:00.
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio is measured. The canary-watch step queries Prometheus every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. Failure is any single reading above 1%, or a query returning no data, which fails it at once and triggers canary-off.
sonnet.q11: The run posts to the #deploys channel (waiting for approval notice) with IMAGE_TAG, a link to the smoke results, and the commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG.
sonnet.q12: Run kubectl rollout undo (in production followed by canary-off), which returns the environment to the pods that were running. Rollback is not used because SSM was not written, so it still names those pods, and rollback's previous_tag would go one version too far back.
